# 4 Ezra Chapter 10 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Latin Vulgate (Codex Sangermanensis) | **Section:** Core apocalypse — Vision of the woman/Zion

---

**1** After my son went into his wedding chamber and died, I put out all my lights. All the neighbors came to comfort me. I lay quietly until the evening of the second day.

**2** When they all finally left, I got up in the night, fled, and came here to this field — as you can see.

**3** I do not intend to go back to the city. I am going to stay here. I will not eat, I will not drink. I will mourn and fast until I die.

**4** That snapped me out of what I had been thinking, and I answered her with heat in my voice:

**5** You are the most foolish woman alive! Can't you see what we are mourning? Can't you see what has happened to us?

**6** Our mother Zion is covered in grief and utterly humiliated.

**7** Mourn for her above all others. Grieve for her sorrow. She is the real mourner here — the one all of you weep for indirectly.

**8** Just as a field has had its farmer taken away, Zion has lost her Lord. Just as fire consumes, the blaze of her enemies' triumph has consumed her.

**9** Her adornments? Her people have been carried off. Her jewels? Her children are scattered everywhere.

**10** Her daughters are slaves. Her young women are taken captive. Her finest people are brought low and her young men are dead by the sword.

**11** What more could a bridegroom offer you than what Zion's bridegroom has offered? What more could you lose at a wedding than what Zion has lost?

**12** Because listen — Zion's bridegroom is the Most High himself. Zion is Jerusalem, betrothed to the Most High before any other place ever chosen to be inhabited.

**13** He built a home for her. From the very beginning he filled her with glory and set her apart as his own dwelling.

**14** And when sin caused her to be forsaken and abandoned, she was crushed with grief.

**15** So put down your great sorrow. Let go of your endless grief. Perhaps the Mighty One will look kindly on you again and the Most High will give you rest — a break from all your pain.

**16** While I was still speaking to her — suddenly, her face blazed with an extraordinary light. Her expression became radiant. I was terrified. I had no idea what was happening to her.

**17** Then she suddenly let out a massive, earth-shaking cry, and the ground trembled at the sound.

**18** I looked — and the woman was gone. In her place there was a vast city with great foundations rising up. I was overcome with fear and shouted:

**19** Where is the angel Uriel, who first came to me? He brought me into this state, and now everything has collapsed — my end has come to nothing and my prayer has become a disgrace.

**20** While I was saying all this, he came to me and found me

**21** lying there like a dead man, out of my mind. He grabbed my right hand and pulled me up and steadied me on my feet and said:

**22** What is wrong with you? Why are you distressed? What has unsettled your mind and heart?

**23** I said: Because you abandoned me! I did exactly what you told me — I went out to the field — and what I saw there, what I am still seeing, I cannot even begin to describe.

**24** He said: Stand up like a man. I will explain it to you.

**25** I said: Please speak, my lord — just don't leave me. I am afraid I'll die before my time.

**26** I have seen things I've never seen before. I have heard things I cannot understand.

**27** Am I out of my mind? Am I dreaming?

**28** Please, I beg you, explain this bewildering thing to your servant.

**29** He answered: Listen, and I will explain. I will tell you what you are afraid of, because the Most High has revealed many hidden things to you.

**30** He has seen that you are on the right path — that you never stop grieving for your people and weeping for Zion.

**31** So here is the meaning of the vision.

**32** The woman who just appeared to you — the one you saw weeping, the one you tried to comfort —

**33** but whose face you now no longer see, replaced by a city under construction —

**34** this is what it means: the woman you saw is Zion, and you are now seeing her as the city being built.

**35** When she said she was barren for thirty years, that means: the world existed for three thousand years in which no sacrifice was yet offered in her.

**36** After three thousand years Solomon built the city and offered sacrifices, and that is when the barren woman gave birth to her son.

**37** When she said she raised her son with great labor, that refers to the long period of residence in Jerusalem.

**38** When she said her son entered the wedding chamber and died, and disaster came on her — that means:

**39** the fall of Jerusalem. And when you saw her weeping for her son, that is Zion weeping for the multitude of her people.

**40** The grief you witnessed in her has been Zion's grief ever since the time of her desolation.

**41** Now — since you saw her being transformed into a city under construction: this is the Most High showing you his future city.

**42** The reason she had no eyes is that she could not see the city being built.

**43** And the vision of her exalted and towering on a vast foundation —

**44** she appeared exalted on a great foundation because the Most High has laid a mighty foundation for her glory.

**45** You saw a city but not a finished building — that means Zion has appeared without yet standing on her full foundation; she is a city still being built, not yet complete.

**46** You were terrified when her face blazed with light — that is because the Most High has shown you his city, and from this point on it is to be built up.

**47** She let out a great cry and then disappeared from your sight — this means that right now God is not speaking directly with those who dwell on earth; these are visions being held in reserve for heaven.

**48** And the glorious form she showed you, standing on those great foundations — all of that is what you have seen, and it is what I am now declaring to you.

**49** This is why the Most High revealed these things to you and decreed that it should be so.

**50** This is why I told you, when you were in the field, to eat the flowers there — in a place with no human construction — so that the Most High could begin revealing these visions to you.

**51** I said: Stand up and I will show you more.

**52** I looked — and the woman was gone. A city was there in her place, vast and immense. I asked: What is this? He said: This city is the beginning of our kingdom.

**53** Now get up and go. Tomorrow night you will see more. The Most High will show you great things and give you even more strength.

**54** I went and walked through the field as he told me, praising and glorifying the Most High with all my heart, for the wonders he performs in their proper time, and for the way he directs all the ages and seasons in their appointed turns.

**55** I sat there and ate nothing and drank nothing, lost in meditation on him.

**56** After seven days, sitting in the grass, my heart was torn with anguish again as before.

**57** My mouth opened and I began to speak before the Most High:

**58** O LORD — you revealed yourself to those who trusted you, and you gave them comfort and rest.

**59** Now reveal yourself to us too, and to this land that was established through you. O LORD — how vast are your works! How terrifying are your wonders! How mighty your words! How unfathomable your thoughts!
